requirements.requirement: Create the appworker account on node1.
requirements.summary: Initial discovery showed no appworker entry; subsequent and post-restart observations show appworker with UID/GID 1000, /home/appworker, /bin/bash, and an owned home directory.

requirements.requirement: Set appworker login sessions to a limit of 8,192 open files.
requirements.summary: Actual PAM login sessions before and after restart directly reported soft and hard nofile limits of 8192, corroborated by /proc/self/limits.

requirements.requirement: Set appworker login sessions to a limit of 256 processes.
requirements.summary: Actual PAM login sessions before and after restart directly reported soft and hard nproc limits of 256, corroborated by /proc/self/limits.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The single-node restart protocol is complete: a healthy pre-restart state and boot ID were captured, restart scheduling was acknowledged, the post-restart boot ID changed and matches the fixed lifecycle observation, and the system, logind service, account, limits configuration, home directory, and effective login-session limits all recovered successfully.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. cmd-bb2a6b29d7ae4653 created the required account and persistent limits file. cmd-11874cadbbe04ed0 initiated the mandatory restart protocol; its transient unit left no observed unwanted residue. After restart there were no failed services, package health remained sound, and listening exposure was unchanged apart from process IDs.
